newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan unions confirm Aug 6 work stoppage.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan unions confirm Aug 6 work stoppage.

text.p: Venezuela's main unions confirmed Friday they would carry out a 12-hour national work stoppage August 6 despite procuring a renewed commitment from business leaders that private sector wages will be raised soon.

"We ratify the national work stoppage for August 6," Federico Ramirez Leon, president of the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV) told reporters after a meeting of union, business and government leaders.
At the meeting, described as "positive" by all sides, business chamber leaders promised to identify businesses that had not met a commitment to raise salaries and force them to comply.
"We are increasing salaries and we will continue to increase salaries across the country," said Francisco Natera, head of Venezuela's largest business chamber Fedecamaras.
Union and government officials have accused the private sector of not complying with a commitment to raise salaries contained in an agreement to reform Venezuela's severance payments system.
Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said it was clear from Friday's meeting that business chamber leaders were committed to raising salaries.
Petkoff said that Wednesday's work stoppage was a legitimate means of pressure by the unions and urged private sector workers to confront their employers over salary rises.
"The private sector workers, unionized or not, have to take action to pressure their bosses for their rights," he said.
No time period had been set for business to hike wages but it should be within 15 days to a month, Petkoff said.
Ramirez Leon, meanwhile, said that for the unions time had already run out and the wage rises must come as soon as possible.
